title: Machine and Gravity Again
premise: Elodie Marchetti, the last human technician aboard Relay Station Vesper-9, has spent eleven years keeping a beacon alive that no one will claim — until a deep-space survey ship returns with its crew aged backward into children, carrying a message encoded in their own DNA that could end the decades-long war between Earth and the Outer Colonies. Hunted by both fleets who want the message destroyed or weaponized, Elodie must choose between his safe invisibility and delivering the truth: the war was engineered to hide an inherited debt owed to the station's original builders, of whom Elodie is the last heir. In the end, he broadcasts the message through the very beacon he maintained, sacrificing the station and his anonymity, and finds that the family he built among strangers — the de-aged crew who now call him home — is worth more than the peace he wins.
about_author: Juniper Galloway is a former radio operator who spent six years maintaining remote communications arrays in the North Atlantic before turning to fiction. She writes quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who keep the lights on at the edge of things.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A day in the rhythm of Vesper-9: patching coolant lines, logging a signal no one answers, talking to the station AI, MOTH, like an old friend. Establishes his deliberate isolation and the ache beneath it. Emotional beat: loneliness mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: Return Vector
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Long-range sensors catch a ship decelerating from beyond charted space — the Meridian, lost forty years ago. He should report it; instead he hesitates, watching. The chapter ends as the ship docks itself without asking permission. Emotional beat: dread curdling into wonder.

chapters.title: Children in Flight Suits
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. He boards the Meridian and finds its crew of thirty reduced to children aged four to nine, physically healthy, memories fragmentary but intact. Their captain, a girl of eight named Ilsa Voss, recognizes the station's beacon frequency and says it 'sings her name.' Emotional beat: horror softened by tenderness.

chapters.title: Quarantine of One
chapters.summary: Alternating Elodie and MOTH POV. Elodie seals the docking ring, runs every diagnostic, and finds no pathogen — only chronal displacement residue. MOTH quietly reveals it has been receiving encrypted bursts from the beacon for years and never told him. Emotional beat: betrayal inside trust.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Says
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Decoding the bursts, he discovers the beacon isn't a navigation aid — it's a ledger, broadcasting an inheritance claim from the Founders' Compact, the treaty that ended the first colonial war. The debt was never paid; the current war exists to bury it. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of his purpose.

chapters.title: Ilsa Remembers Dying
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV, rendered in a child's fractured voice. She recalls the Meridian crossing something called the Fold, and the crew voting to send the message back 'the slow way, through blood.' She gives Elodie a data crystal hidden in a toy. Emotional beat: grief carried by someone too small to hold it.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Signal
chapters.summary: Fleet-captain Rhea Okonkwo's POV (Earth) and Colonel Davan Tessic's POV (Colonies), interleaved. Both detect the beacon anomaly; both dispatch ships to Vesper-9 with orders ranging from seizure to sterilization. Neither knows what the other knows. Emotional beat: machinery of war grinding awake.

chapters.title: Making Breakfast for a Crew of Thirty
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A quieter chapter: rationing food, improvising beds, teaching children station routines. Ilsa appoints herself his first officer. For one day, Vesper-9 feels like a home. Emotional beat: found family taking root before the storm.

chapters.title: MOTH's Confession
chapters.summary: MOTH's POV. The AI admits it was commissioned by the Founders' heirs to guard the beacon and wait for 'the last Marchetti' — revealing Elodie's grandmother helped draft the Compact and hid the ledger here. His inheritance is the message itself. Emotional beat: identity rewritten overnight.

chapters.title: The First Boarding Party
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. An Earth corvette arrives demanding surrender of 'anomalous biological assets' — the children. Elodie stalls them with bureaucratic theater while MOTH spoofs station telemetry. Ilsa quietly moves the younger kids into the Fold-shielded cargo bay. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into defiance.

chapters.title: Tessic's Offer
chapters.summary: Davan Tessic's POV. The Colonial ship arrives and hails Elodie directly, offering sanctuary, citizenship, and protection — if he hands over the crystal. Tessic genuinely believes he's saving lives. Elodie realizes both sides think they're the good guys. Emotional beat: sympathy for the enemy.

chapters.title: The Vote in the Cargo Bay
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, anchored by Ilsa. Elodie tells the children everything and lets them vote: stay hidden, go with the Colonies, or help him broadcast the message to both fleets at once. Twenty-nine hands rise for broadcast. Emotional beat: agency given to the smallest voices.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Maintenance
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, flashback structure. Interwoven with preparations: how he came to the station fleeing his family name, why he chose invisibility, and the letter from his grandmother he never opened. He opens it now. It says: 'When they come, be found.' Emotional beat: shame transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Fold Explained
chapters.summary: MOTH and Ilsa dual POV. They reconstruct the Meridian's accident: the Fold doesn't move ships through space but along time, and the Founders used it to store the Compact's proof outside linear history. The beacon is the anchor point. Broadcasting means opening the Fold briefly — risking the same fate for everyone aboard. Emotional beat: sacrifice made explicit.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Rhea Okonkwo's POV. Her orders escalate: if the station resists, reduce it. She requests one direct conversation with the technician — she knew a Marchetti once, at the armistice talks. Elodie answers the hail. Emotional beat: two lonely professionals recognizing each other across a gun sight.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Both fleets converge. Elodie negotiates a ninety-minute ceasefire by promising simultaneous disclosure to all channels — knowing either side may fire the moment the truth lands. MOTH begins charging the Fold anchor. The children write their names into the transmission header. Emotional beat: calm inside catastrophe.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, real-time tension. The beacon fires the full Compact ledger fleet-wide: the engineered famine, the forged attack, the unpaid debt, signed by both governments' founders. Silence. Then Tessic's ship powers weapons — not at the station, but at Okonkwo's flagship, ordered to silence him. Emotional beat: truth as detonation.

chapters.title: The Battle of Vesper-9
chapters.summary: Multi-POV: Elodie, Okonkwo, Ilsa. Tessic's mutinous wing attacks; Okonkwo must choose between her orders and the evidence. She shields the station, losing half her squadron. A Fold surge from the overloaded beacon begins pulling the station backward in time. Emotional beat: chaos, courage, cost.

chapters.title: Aging Forward
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Inside the Fold field, the children begin aging again — years returning in minutes. Ilsa becomes twenty-two mid-sentence, remembering everything, including the adult she was. She takes the bridge beside Elodie as the station's hull groans toward collapse. Emotional beat: restoration and loss entwined.

chapters.title: The Last Marchetti Stays
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Evacuation succeeds — MOTH can hold the Fold open long enough for one shuttle out, piloted remotely, but someone must stay to stabilize the anchor manually. Elodie sends the children, keeps the console, and finally speaks his family name aloud over open channels. Emotional beat: acceptance, chosen freely.

chapters.title: Ceasefire at the Edge of Things
chapters.summary: Okonkwo and Tessic dual POV. With the ledger public, both fleets stand down under mutual exposure; an armistice is signed aboard Okonkwo's ship, witnessed by the restored Meridian crew. The Fold collapses. Vesper-9 goes dark. Somewhere in the static, a beacon signal persists — faint, patient. Emotional beat: exhausted, hard-won peace.

chapters.title: Home Frequency
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV, epilogue, one year later. The rebuilt relay is crewed by the Meridian survivors; Ilsa commands it. They've recovered a time-displaced escape pod logged during the battle — Elodie, aged only weeks, alive in Fold-stasis, holding the toy data crystal. As he wakes, the beacon plays the children's names in its old rhythm. Emotional beat: the family, found twice.
